To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the pion mass decreases with temperature and vanishes at a temperature of about 150 MeV, 2) the pion decreases with density and vanishes at densities of about 2 times nuclear matter densities, and 3) the pion-nucleon coupling constant increases with both temperature and density.
the pion mass decreases with temperature and density.
The pion mass is reduced by explicit chiral symmetry-breaking effects in the vacuum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the low-temperature and low-density behavior of the pion.
the low temperature variation in the pionic mass, and its relation to the density dependence of this mass.
a study of the pion as a probe of the chiral phase transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
at finite density and temperature, the pion mass is a rapidly varying function of both variables.
the pion mass at finite temperature and finite density is very different from the pion mass in vacuum.
the pion mass decreases with density at least as much as the nucleon mass increases with density, and perhaps more so.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pion is the only light meson whose mass is significantly affected by temperature and density.

the pion mass is expected to decrease with increasing density, but increase with increasing temperature, at least in the region of moderate temperature and density changes, where the quark condensation is still significant.
the pion-nucleus interaction at zero temperature and finite density, as well as the pion-nuclear interaction at finite temperature and zero density, are both weak.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion mass is not a fixed parameter in the QCD phase diagram, but rather a variable that depends on the temperature, density, and chemical potentials of the system.
the pion mass decreases rapidly with increasing density.
the pion mass is a very sensitive thermometer and barometer.
